reviewer: authoring agent, on Arena.ai; no second human reviewer
outcome_explanation: Every automated check passes, including the SVD construction, the existence-condition counterexamples, the norm identities, the square-root general form, and the measured breakdown of the A'A construction. The lesson is nevertheless NOT marked verified, because source fidelity has not been checked by a human reader and publication integrity is untested (no interface was rendering this lesson when the record was written). Marking it verified would assert something that did not happen.

checks.name: source_fidelity
checks.method: Not performed by a human reader. The lesson was written against MML sections 4.3-4.5 and 4.7 (printed pp.114-134) with the section text available during writing, and it states explicitly where the source proves a result and where it leaves the proof to the reader (Cholesky existence, Theorem 4.18) or states it without proof (Eckart-Young, reserved for the next lesson).
checks.evidence: Cited identifiers were checked to exist in knowledge/sources/mml/inventory.json (Definitions 4.19, 4.23; Theorems 4.18, 4.20, 4.21, 4.22, 4.24; Figure 4.8), which is automated and passes. Whether the explanations are a fair representation of the source has not been independently reviewed.
checks.not_checked: Whether a reader of MML would agree with the emphasis and the omissions, in particular the decision to present the SVD derivation with the steps the source compresses.

checks.name: technical_correctness
checks.method: Every numerical and algebraic claim in the lesson and its solutions was recomputed by content/checks/math07_svd_checks.py using sympy (exact) and numpy (floating point), and the checks were executed by tools/run_content_checks.py.
checks.evidence: 8 checks in this module, all passing; 17 checks in the suite, 0 failures. Recorded output: knowledge/lessons/checks-report.json. Notable measured values: the textbook SVD construction matches numpy to 4.3e-13 on well-conditioned inputs and loses all digits at a singular-value ratio of 1e10.
checks.not_checked: The numerical experiments sample random matrices; they do not establish worst-case behaviour, which would require condition-number analysis rather than sampling.

checks.name: mathematical_validity
checks.method: The constructive SVD proof was written out in full and its five steps checked against the objects they claim to construct: A'A is symmetric positive semi-definite and its eigenvalues are non-negative (verified symbolically), the u_i are orthonormal (verified exactly), AA'u_i = sigma_i^2 u_i (used and implied by the exact reconstruction test), U completes to an orthogonal basis (verified exactly), and U Sigma V' = A in exact arithmetic on two examples.
checks.evidence: check_ex02_full_svd_3x2 and check_lesson_worked_examples verify the 3x2 and the 2x2 examples exactly; check_ex01 verifies the Cholesky factor and the pivot argument; check_ex06 verifies the general square-root form exactly, including the orthogonality of W.
checks.not_checked: Two statements are cited rather than proved: the rank-nullity counting in exercise 5 uses rank(A'A) = rank(A), which is shown for the example and asserted in general; and the uniqueness of the triangular square root is asserted in the solution, which says so.

checks.name: pedagogical_completeness
checks.method: Mapped each of the lesson's three declared outcomes to the sections that teach it and to exercises that assess it.
checks.evidence: Outcome 1 (existence conditions with counterexamples) is taught in sections 1.1, 2 and 4 and assessed by exercises 1 and 3. Outcome 2 (SVD as rotation, scaling, rotation) is taught in section 3.3 with the worked example in 3.4 and assessed by exercise 2. Outcome 3 (relating the SPD eigendecomposition to the Cholesky factor) is taught in section 2 and assessed by exercise 6, which establishes the precise relation rather than the common misstatement.
checks.not_checked: Whether the ordering serves a first-time reader; the lesson assumes the eigenvalue material is fresh.

checks.name: prerequisite_integrity
checks.method: Listed the prerequisites and the specific fact each supplies, and checked that each is defined in the framework and fully sourced by the supplied book.
checks.evidence: MATH-06 (eigenvalues and the spectral theorem, covered by LSN-MATH-06-01), MATH-04 (orthogonality, MML sections 3.1-3.6) and MATH-02 (matrices as mappings, MML 2.2-2.8). All three are declared 'sourced' in coverage.json and precede section 4.3 in the book's own order.
checks.not_checked: Whether the learner has completed them.

checks.name: assessment_integrity
checks.method: Every exercise has an expected outcome, a difficulty, a declared origin and a solution; every solution names its method and its verification.
checks.evidence: 7 exercises: 6 original, 1 adapted with the source item recorded (MML exercises 4.8/4.9, printed p.138). Exercise 7 carries a rubric. Four source exercises (4.8, 4.9, 4.11, 4.12) and one that belongs to the next lesson (4.10) are listed as deliberately left unsolved, with the reason stated.
checks.not_checked: Whether a reader other than the author finds the exercises unambiguous.

checks.name: citation_integrity
checks.method: Automated checks that every cited section and numbered object exists in the generated source index, and that every recorded printed page matches the index.
checks.evidence: tools/validate_knowledge.py checks lesson-source-section-exists, lesson-source-anchor-exists and lesson-source-anchor-page-matches-index all pass for this lesson.
checks.not_checked: Whether the source supports the claim being made; that is source_fidelity, which is not run.

checks.name: interactive_correctness
checks.method: This lesson contains no interactive component; the interactive rank-truncation demonstration belongs to LSN-MATH-08-01.
checks.evidence: The lesson contains display mathematics rendered by KaTeX and no client-side component.

checks.name: publication_integrity
checks.method: Not performed when the record was written. The lesson is eligible for rendering (front matter validated, equations and links type-checked by the build), but no rendering test had been run against it.
checks.evidence: The application builds the lesson route without error and the registry validation passes, which is a build-time check only.
checks.not_checked: Equation rendering at small widths, the internal cross-links to LSN-MATH-06-01 and LSN-MATH-08-01, and whether the practice table's anchors land on the right solutions.
